title: Delta3R: Constant-Memory Streaming 3D Reconstruction with a Delta-Rule Scene State
teaser: CUT3R made streaming reconstruction constant-memory with a recurrent scene state; follow-ups recalibrate its update (TTT3R, ReCal3R) or interleave decay-gated linear memories (HorizonStream). This project replaces the cell with Kimi Delta Attention — delta-rule overwrite plus per-channel decay — testing whether re-observations fuse rather than double-count, and whether chunked kernels unlock hundreds-of-frame training.
abstract: CUT3R streams frames against a persistent state at constant memory, and the wave that followed treats that memory as the central problem — StreamVGGT caches keys and values (its cache grows with every frame), TTT3R and ReCal3R re-read CUT3R's update as online learning and calibrate its learning rate, HorizonStream interleaves channel-wise-decay linear attention that stays stable past 10,000 frames. Two failures remain. Additive writes provably interfere on repeated keys — re-observations accumulate instead of fusing — and CUT3R's residual update, read as fixed-rate online gradient descent (TTT3R), shares this write-without-read structure; decay alone forgets indiscriminately, damping still-valid geometry along with stale content. The delta rule is the missing piece: Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), the linear-attention cell of Kimi K3, reads what its matrix state stores under the incoming key and writes back only the difference, scaled by a learned write-strength, while a per-channel decay fades the previous state — read-before-write is fusion, a learned running counterpart of weighted TSDF integration, and exactly what decay-gated memories lack. KDA's chunked kernels (fla) also train the recurrence on hundreds of frames at once, where backpropagation-through-time caps CUT3R's training at short windows. We swap CUT3R's state update for a KDA cell, distill from the frozen model on short clips, then train long on ScanNet++ walkthroughs; encoders and decoders stay frozen. The scientific questions are sharp: (i) does a delta-rule state improve re-visited regions where additive and decay-only cells drift or double-count, isolated by swapping only the update rule at matched parameters; (ii) do per-channel gate statistics segment static from dynamic content without supervision; (iii) does long-chunk training buy anything beyond short-clip generalization — in particular on revisit consistency, which decay cannot fix; (iv) does memory stay flat at StreamVGGT-class accuracy? Kernels are Triton and run on lab GPUs. A K3-style hybrid — sparse exact-attention layers over a bounded keyframe bank for loop closure — is the stretch goal.
milestones: Literature review (the linear-attention memory ladder — linear attention, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, KDA/Kimi Linear; the streaming-reconstruction wave — CUT3R, StreamVGGT, TTT3R, ReCal3R, Mamba-VGGT, HorizonStream); stand up CUT3R inference and evaluation (video depth, pose, pointmap accuracy/completeness), profile memory and accuracy versus sequence length, and mine revisit segments from ScanNet++ ground-truth poses (frustum overlap between temporally distant frames). Kill test: on a synthetic key-value revisit task, verify the three memory rules fail exactly as predicted — additive double-counts re-observations, scalar decay damages untouched entries, the delta rule fuses — before any 3D training.

The cell swap at small scale: integrate a KDA cell (fla's chunk_kda / fused_recurrent_kda; pin fla and Triton versions and verify forward/backward on an A6000 in week one) as CUT3R's state update — image tokens write key-value pairs into the matrix state, queries read it back, starting from the simplest placement: a single cell replacing the state-token cross-attention at one interaction point — keeping encoder and decoders frozen; distill frozen CUT3R's pointmaps and poses on short (up to 64-frame) clips until the swap comes within roughly 10 percent of the baseline.

Long-sequence training with the chunked kernel on 200-500-frame ScanNet++ walkthrough clips — per-chunk gradient checkpointing, loss on a subsampled frame set, encoder features precomputed offline, and a 224-resolution fallback if memory demands it; evaluate the long-horizon regime: drift (ATE), accuracy/completeness versus frame count, memory-versus-length curves against CUT3R and StreamVGGT, and revisit consistency (reconstruction error on re-visited regions, second pass versus first). Milestones 1-3 are a self-contained Guided Research / IDP scope.

The controlled comparison the field is missing: delta rule versus additive versus decay-only (HorizonStream-style) state cells, and per-channel versus scalar gating, at matched parameters and training compute; write-strength analysis (does it track observation quality — blur, parallax, occlusion?) and zero-shot gate-statistics analysis on the Bonn and TUM dynamic sequences from CUT3R's evaluation suite (does static/dynamic factorization emerge?).

(Stretch) Loop-closure hybrid: add sparse exact-attention layers over a bounded keyframe token bank (K3-style ~3:1 interleave) and test whether a few exact-recall layers recover offline-level revisit accuracy while streaming memory stays constant; or extend the evaluation to full dynamic (4D) reconstruction.
